subject.title: feat(agents): configured agent env reaches spawned subprocesses

question: Should OpenClaw accept broad literal `agents.list[].env` for CLI, exec, ACP/ACPX, and stdio MCP subprocesses, or prefer the narrower SecretRef/exec-only contract in PR #96309?
rationale: The patch adds a credential-adjacent public config surface and changes subprocess env precedence across several runtime owners, and automation cannot choose the permanent product/security boundary.

options.title: Choose the canonical env contract first
options.body: Resolve broad literal per-agent env versus the narrower SecretRef/exec-only model, then merge only the branch that matches that decision.

options.title: Accept this broad contract
options.body: Treat this PR as the canonical sanitized child-process env surface after the generated docs map is repaired and required checks are satisfactory.

options.title: Pause for the alternative path
options.body: Keep this PR open or close it later only if the exec-only SecretRef path becomes the accepted and merged implementation.

recommendation.title: Choose the canonical env contract first
recommendation.body: Resolve broad literal per-agent env versus the narrower SecretRef/exec-only model, then merge only the branch that matches that decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor requested this review based on prior guidance, and recent history ties this handle to config, exec, and ACPX-adjacent surfaces.
